hints.title: Ten Character Window Recurrence
hints.text: Substrings of length ten can appear more than once in a longer genetic string. How can tracking strings encountered so far distinguish first appearances from recurring ones?

hints.title: Window Slicing Seen Invariant
hints.text: Scanning windows of length ten from index 0 to length minus ten and recording occurrences in a collection highlights duplicates without re-scanning.

hints.title: Double Collection Deduplication Procedure
hints.text: Initialize two collections for seen sequences and duplicates. Slide a ten-character slice across the string from index 0 up to length minus ten. If the slice already exists in seen, add it to duplicates; otherwise, record it in seen. Return the collected duplicate strings as a list.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing every 10-character substring with every other 10-character substring takes O(N^2) time and quadratic string comparisons.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking seen substrings in a hash set runs in O(N * L) time where L = 10, using O(N * L) space to store the substrings.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should identify the fixed window length L=10 and mention bitmask rolling hash (2 bits per nucleotide) as a further memory optimization.
